title: Introduce multi-window token-surge detector and contextual log weaver
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a multi-window token surge detector and a contextual log weaver. Adds new alerting rules and a dashboard panel. Backwards compatible; rollout staged behind an observability feature flag.
body: Motivation: customer-facing incidents in late Jan showed short-lived token surges that caused transient SLO breaches. Existing p95/p99 checks reacted too coarsely — we need a detector that reasons about slope and burst shape across short, medium, and long windows and ties signal to logs for rapid RCA. This PR implements a multi-window token-surge detector (1m/5m/1h windows with exponential decay), a surge-score combining slope + burst persistence, and a contextual log weaver that stitches deferred log fragments to invocations using invocation-id + kv-hash anchors. Design summary: - Token-surge detector: sliding exponentially-weighted counters per route/tenant, computes instantaneous rate, short-window slope, persistence score, and produces a compact surge-score (0-100). Configurable thresholds (warn/critical) are exposed as alert bindings. - Multi-window logic: 3 windows (1m, 5m, 1h) with tunable decay factors. Detector outputs both raw time-series (for dashboards) and discrete surge events (for alert rules). - Contextual log weaver: consumes deferred logs and partial spans from the telemetry pipeline, uses deterministic anchors (invocation-id, kv-prefetch-hash, token-range) to join fragments and produce a fused context payload attached to the surge event. The weaver is opt-in and respects PII redaction rules and KMS tagging. - Alerting: new alert rule token-surge-rule.yaml implements staged alerting with quiet windows and priority-based dampening. When a tenant has frequent false positives, quieting escalates from warn->silent->backoff. - Dashboard: Adds a surge-cluster panel (sparkline of surge-score + burst clusters), per-tenant heatmap, and an interactive trace link that opens the fused log context. - Rollout: feature-flagged, canary to 10% traffic, then 50% and 100% after 48h of low false-positive rate. Includes a kill-switch to disable the weaver if log join rate exceeds budget. Backwards compatibility: No API changes to external customers. Internal metrics names are additive; defaults preserve prior alert behavior. Testing & validation: - Unit tests for slope estimator and decay math - Integration tests that replay synthetic token bursts and verify surge-score shape - E2E canary run in perf-lab with traffic mixed across short/long sequences - Load bench: added benchmark that simulates 2k TPS of small invocations; detector adds ~2% CPU at typical 95th load. Security & privacy: weaver respects existing redaction and never exports raw PII; fused context payloads are encrypted in transit and tagged for audit. Migration notes: Operators can tune windows and thresholds via console under Observability->Anomaly Detectors. The feature is configurable per-tenant. Checklist: - [x] Detector core implementation - [x] Weaver pipeline and joiner - [x] Dashboard panels - [x] Alert rules and quieting logic - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Canary rollout plan - [x] Runbooks and README (telemetry/weaver/README.md) Related work: This complements ENG-9142 (alert dampening refactor) and extends ENG-9531 (token cost attribution).
